task.description:
Combined Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) per WF-03_issue_resolving.md. Claim this handoff by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.

Step 0.5: search docs/issues/*.yaml for a resolved entry with matching symptoms -- ISS-0329 (parallel test schema/connection isolation, resolved 2026-08-24) is the closest prior candidate; read its resolution and state whether this is the same root cause recurring (if so, bump severity to at least MAJOR) or a distinct mechanism.

Step 1: Reproduce directly under scripts/test_parallel.sh repeatedly (standalone `mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs` already confirmed clean by ORCH -- 4/4 passed -- so do NOT rely on a standalone run; you must reproduce under actual parallel partitioning). Read test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's provisioned_tenant!/1 (Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) called globally) and trace how this interacts with other concurrently-running async tests/partitions when test_parallel.sh spawns N separate `mix test --partitions N` OS processes. Determine: is this a cross-PROCESS issue (each partition is a separate BEAM VM against the same physical Postgres, so Sandbox :auto in one partition process cannot leak into another process's connections) or a cross-test-WITHIN-partition issue (an async test in the SAME partition process racing against this async:false test's global Sandbox mode flip)? Quote real reproduction output -- run scripts/test_parallel.sh at least 3 times if the first doesn't reproduce it, since ISS-0329/ISS-0340's own history shows this class of failure is itself flaky (different counts/sets across identical runs). Do NOT implement a fix -- produce the diagnosis for CODE-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: docs/issues/*.yaml searched, ISS-0329 specifically read and compared, finding (recurrence or distinct) stated explicitly
the failure reproduced under real scripts/test_parallel.sh parallel execution with real quoted output, not just asserted from the original PR's report
root cause traced to a specific mechanism (cross-process vs. cross-test-within-partition, or another mechanism if evidence points elsewhere) -- not asserted, demonstrated
no fix implemented; next_action names CODE-DESIGNER (or, if this turns out to be a test-infra-only issue needing no application-code design, states that explicitly and names the direct next step)
